title: your life in Warhammer 40k (Space Marine)
fullText: You weren't born. Okay, of of course you were born. This is Warhammer 40k. Your luck wasn't landing you as Jesus. You were born screaming, covered in blood, and probably already being judged by a servo skull with a clipboard. But that part where you got to be a person, that ended fast because someone looked at your orphaned, half feral 13-year-old self and thought, "Yeah, let's give that kid acid spit and a rocket launcher." First the tests, then the surgery, then the upgrades. They installed 19 organs. Not metaphorically. They literally opened you up and started adding them. One lets you eat poison. One lets you breathe in space. One lets you lick dirt and taste its feelings. Science. Then they staple the black carropus into your spine, turning your body into a USB port for power armor. From that point on, you didn't wear armor. You were armor. If it itched, too bad. If it pinched, that's loyalty. They erased your name, called it purity. They erase your memories. Called it devotion. Your personality unnecessary variance. You got assigned to a legion. Not chosen, assigned to none other than the ultramarines. The blue ones. The noble ones. The ones who print their battle plans on parchment and then light it on fire for extra purity. You didn't feel noble. You just felt heavy. You met your squad in a training cage. No names, just chain weapons and trauma. One of them hadn't blinked in 3 weeks. One quoted scripture in his sleep. One kept talking to his boulder like it was his dead twin. You learn fast because asking questions got you re-evaluated and re-evaluation meant getting stabbed and replaced by the next get in line. You were told this was brotherhood. It mostly felt like structured emotional damage. They taught you how to fight before you learned how to eat slowly. They taught you how to chant before you understood half the words. And when your bones broke, good. Now you could learn how to fight while healing. Eventually, you earned your first deployment. Great crusade they called it. Thousands of worlds reunited with the Imperium. Thousands of cultures that didn't want to be. You were told to bring unity. You brought a bolter and righteous indignation. Your first kill was a rebel who called the emperor overrated. Your second was a child with a plasma gun and too much hope. You told yourself it was for the Imperium. It tasted like burning oil and moral flexibility. You saw your primarch once. Rabote Gilaman, the avenging son, built like a cathedral and glowing like someone who always files taxes early. He didn't see you. He saw the formation, but you stood straighter anyway. They said he was your gene father. But you didn't feel still, you believed in the emperor, in the mission, in the idea that all this pain had a purpose. Because if you stopped believing even for a second, you might remember what it felt like to be human. And that would be worse. So, you kept marching, kept telling yourself that all is well. And for a while, it actually felt like it was working. The Emperor had a plan. The galaxy had a structure. Your squad only stabbed each other during training drills. Sure, the Great Crusade was mostly yelling and compliance bullets, but at least it was organized yelling. Then, your cousin Legion stopped responding to Vox calls. Then, another one showed up to a war zone with a new logo and way too much eyeliner. Then, someone whispered, "What if dad's just wrong?" And next thing you know, you're getting deployed to remind your own gan brothers what loyalty means with a bolter. But hey, at least you aren't captaining a 10,000 ton warship through a thunderstorm while dodging torpedoes and trying not to disappoint the man who built half the US Navy out of spite because that's naval combat. And that's what you get in World of Warships, today's sponsor. This free-to-play tactical game lets you command real US ships like the USS Albany and USS Smith recreated from actual 20th century blueprints. There are over 40 maps, seven battle types, and weather that actually changes how you fight. Ships are split into four classes. Battleships hit hard and take hits harder. Destroyers are fast, sneaky, and allergic to staying alive. Cruisers do a bit of everything and get blamed when it all goes wrong. And carriers just press buttons from across the map and pretend it's strategy. Right now, there's a Fourth of July event running featuring limited time US ships, stars, and stripe skins, and enough firepower to make even new players a threat. So, if you want to command actual Maval history instead of getting vaporized in a cutscene, click the link in the description or Ben Comeded and use code step up to get 7 days premium, 1 million credits, 500 Deloons, USS Albany, and USS Smith for free. It's on PC and console. And unlike many clickbait games, World of Warships is free. So, yeah, the only heresy here is not clicking the link. Grab your fleet, claim your rewards, and use code stepup while the Fourth of July events still live. Now, back to the cousin on cousin trauma. You thought the Xenos were bad. Try explaining betrayal to someone who shares your chin structure and war crimes resume. You were promised unity. What you got was cousin on cousin warfare and the galaxy's worst family reunion. One minute you're chanting war hymns with a guy over a ration brick shaped like guilt. The next he's across the battlefield wearing the same armor just slightly moodier whispering about how the emperor isn't who he's used to be. You shoot him in the throat. He doesn't flinch until the second shot. You don't even know if that counts as heresy or just extremely aggressive disagreement. That's the moment the galaxy flips and we call it the Horus heresy. Like branding the end of sanity makes it easier to file. Half the legions go full cult. One Primark stubs his ego and suddenly you're being told to reunite at Bolter Point. Horus betrays the emperor. The Council of Na abands librarians. Nobody checks the math on that. Now every third psycher is auditioning for a warp themed exorcism speedrun. and you're stuck babysitting a chaplain who thinks PTSD is a training opportunity. Your sergeant calls it a civil war. The chaplain calls it divine testing. You just call it Thursday. You're deployed against the sons of Horus. They don't wear Luna Wolf White anymore to see green and spite. You recognize one of them. You train together on that moon with the servo drones that kept electrocuting people for character. He helped you bury one. You don't bury him. You vaporize what's left. Burn the soil and keep moving. Loyalty used to be simple. Now the wordbearers are quoting scripture midstabbing. The emperor's children turned civilian torture into performance art. The world eaters gave up grammar entirely and now communicate exclusively through chainsaw decibel levels. One guy in your squad starts muttering about visions. He carves something into his armor and calls it decorative. The chaplain calls it a reason to bring out the flamer. You don't ask questions. You just start cleaning your bolter a little more obsessively. They say the siege of terror is coming. that the Emperor will make a final stand, that this is the moment that defines the Imperium. You're not so sure. You're currently kneede in dead heretics, guarding a trench that smells like burnt prayer scrolls, watching another Thunderhawk crash like divine satire. You reload. You look across the field and lock eyes with another Aardis. Same gate, same armor, same slightly exhausted posture. You shoot first because if you hesitate, you're next. And just like that, it's no longer about crusades or banners or faith. And before you can catch your breath, the call comes down. Terra is under siege. Time to go home, or what's left of it. This is it. The final stand. The moment that saves humanity. You're not in the throne room. You're not even near it. You're three decks down, crawling through sewage tunnels beneath what used to be a museum. Above you, titans fighting like kaijuized divorce lawyers. below you and six exhausted brothers bleeding into trench rot and whispering litinies like they're bug repellent. You hold the line for 13 straight days, not because you're brave, because the medic ran out of stems and figured anyone still moving was fine. You fight through traitors, demons, collapsing infrastructure, and your own growing suspicion that maybe this divine plan was more like a group project where everyone died and the emperor took the credit. Then it happens. They say Horus is dead, that the emperor lives. You don't feel victorious. You just feel tired. You clean your bolter again, eat another ration brick shaped like a purity seal, and wait for someone to tell you what's next. Nobody does. The psykers go quiet. The chaplain cries for the first time in his life, and pretend it's condensation. The sky looks wrong. You ask if we won. They say, "The emperor endures." which is code for he's been stapled to a throne and wired into the psychic mainframe like a divine Wi-Fi router. You don't see his body, but you saw the aftershocks, the silence, the sermons rewritten mid-sentence, the people too scared to ask what alive really means anymore. They say he chose this that he's watching. You look around at the broken wall, the shattered squads, the half-dead world you're now responsible for protecting. But there's no time for grief because the traitors, they're not dead, just running. and the Imperium. It's not victorious. It's about to get rebranded. New banners, new rules, same nightmare. The heresy ends on paper, but the cleanup that's just getting started. They told you Horus was dead, that the Emperor was alive, that the Imperium stood victorious. Then they handed you a flamer and told you to start with your old recruitment planet. This wasn't about justice anymore. This was about optics. The scouring wasn't a war. It was a cleanup. One by one, you chase the traitor legions into the eye of terror. World by world, monument by monument. If it bore the wrong colors, burn it. If it quoted the wrong scripture, burn it. If it didn't cheer loud enough during a compliance parade, double burn. You asked if this was still holy work. The chaplain stared at you so long you started reciting litinies out of guilt. You're given a fresh purity seal and told to stop asking questions. You pin it to your chest like it's supposed to keep the memories from leaking out. Spoiler, it doesn't. The CEX Estardes gets introduced with splits legions into chapters to prevent another Horus, trading might for control. Gilamin writes it. And by writes, we mean data dumps 500 pages of passive aggressive war rules and calls it divine structure. Your job now includes checklists. You used to charge into battle with a chainsord and a scream. Now you submit a formation request and wait for bolter clearance. You lose your first friend to deviation. He wore his old legion tattoo one day too long. Then say he retired. You find his helmet in the supply bin 2 weeks later. Sometimes in the silence between deployments, you find yourself whispering their names. The ones they made you burn. The ones they made you forget. You say them in low Gothic. Quiet just once, then delete them again. Because in the Imperium, memory is a liability. But paperwork, paperwork is sacred now. And your legion not a legion anymore. Now it's a chapter. Same colors. Fear Brothers, more mandatory war chance. Some of your squad got reassigned. Some volunteered to start new chapters. One vanished mid- briefing and came back with a different name and a promotion. No one asked questions. You just called them brother and pretended the old name didn't echo. There were no more glorious crusade charges. Now it's tactical engagement pattern gamma ters. Approved by middle management and blessed by bureaucracy. You used to win battles by instinct. Now you win them by powerpoint. Your captain starts quoting sub clauses midfight. Your sergeant carries a purity checklist. You find yourself missing the days when you just punched heretics and prayed after. Your chapter gets a new chaplain. He's younger than your helmet. Quotes doctrine like slam poetry. Calls the emperor the first spreadsheet. You laugh, then realize he's serious and then cry a little, silently because emotion is still considered a soft mutation. You fight in a dozen more crusades against orcs, Elar, and things so weird the administratum hasn't named them yet. You lose brothers. You gain honors, but you forget what the honors were for. Sometimes you see the others, the new chapters. They share your gene seed, not your memories. You used to feel like a sword. Now you just feel heavier. And I don't mean emotional baggage. Okay, maybe I do. I can't be your narrator and your therapist, so like this one's on you. But hey, that's just aging, right? According to the codeex, you're still combat effective. And if you're not, well, the Imperium has a plan for that, too. You just get repurposed, so you keep going. Decades blur, wars change names, enemies respawn with new hats, and you you've been at war for centuries, or at least it feels like that. you stopped counting somewhere around your 20th compliance campaign or your eighth crusade or maybe it was that one skirmish where your arm got vaporized and the tech marine reattached it using incense, duct tape, and what might have been fake. Point is, you're still here and honestly, you're starting to think that is the punishment. The galaxy keeps changing. New Zenos, new cults, new ways to scream in languages your auto translator actively censors for morale reasons. You once fought a creature that wasn't born in real space. Your captain called it a demon. You called it Tuesday because Thursdays already got booked. The warp storms get worse. Time fractures. One mission takes two hours for you, 12 years for everyone else. You return to base and find out your chapter already mourned you, replaced you, and assigned your bunker to a servtor named Clanky. Clanky snores loudly. You fight alongside new recruits now. Primaris, shinier, taller, built like bad decisions and power armor. They're polite, efficient, soulless. You don't hate them, you just hate that they still believe. Your chaplain starts mumbling during sermons. Your apothecary stops naming the dad and starts assigning serial numbers. You haven't prayed in 38 standard cycles. Not because you lost faith. You just ran out of new material. Sometimes you dream about your old squad. Sometimes you see them on the battlefield. Problem is, you're pretty sure they've been dead for 400 years. You ask the librarian if that's normal. He says define normal. Then his nose starts bleeding. You reload. You fight. You keep going because you're a space marine. You don't get to stop. You barely remember getting reassigned to this new warp mission. One minute you're patching up a bolter with duct tape and sarcasm. The next you're staring out at a pothole at a space that's technically illegal to look at for too long. Great. Warp travel again. You've done this before hundreds of times. You've got the whole routine down. Recite the lities. Bless the toilet. Don't make eye contact with a bulkhead if it starts pulsing. But this time, no screams, no visions, just vibes. bad ones. You tell yourself it's fine. Maybe the Gellerfield just feels extra cursed today. Maybe it's normal for the medic station to hum in harmony with your heartbeat. Maybe the bolter is supposed to whisper your name when you're not holding it. You ask the chaplain. He tells you the emperor protects, then forgets your name, then blesses a vending machine, so you stop asking. Instead, you do what you've always done. Clean your gear. Ignore the walls exhaling like they've got lungs. You start dreaming weird again. Not scary, just familiar. Too familiar. You see old battlefields you don't remember fighting on. Dead brothers saying things you definitely never said, except it still feels like you said them. You chalk it up to stress or time dilation or the emotional equivalent of filing taxes for 900 years straight. The warp doesn't scream this time. It size like it's been watching you this whole time and finally went, "Okay, buddy. You've earned a break." And the worst part, you almost believe it. That the whispering's done. That the worst is over. that you'll finally get to rest, but nope. You wake up to another drop pod, another flame briefing, another heresy. Okay, now you've been fighting for a long time, like long time. You're not sure how long exactly because time has gotten weird. Could be a few centuries, could be brunch. All you know is the bolter still works. The mission isn't over. And some shiny new Promeus just called you ancient like it was a compliment. You keep getting honored. Medals, blessings, purity seals stapled to your chest like divine participation trophies. You haven't taken your armor off in ever, but that's fine. Stardies don't retire. They just get louder when they breathe. Then there's the new guy, wideeyed, fresh jean seed, looks at you like your history class with a pulse. Says something like, "It's an honor to serve beside you, ancient. What's it like being awake?" You laugh, except you don't. Your box speaker clicks. The kid salutes and walks away thinking he heard divine static. You sit there wondering when your voice stopped working. You chalk it up to warp trauma. Maybe spiritual compression. Maybe the armor is just extra creaky today. You've been through worse. Like that one battle you half remember where your chest blade got split open and your legs stopped working and someone whispered, "We can still use him." Then nothing. Anyway, no time to dwell. There's heresy to extinguish. Mid battle, mid flamethrower burst, you turn toward a shattered wall panel. It reflects just enough light for you to see. A sarcophagus wired up like a cathedral fuse box. Fists the size of jet bikes. Legs bolted to a mech frame. Your frame. Oh. Huh. You're a dreadnot. Okay. Cool. Cool. Cool. Cool. Cool. That explains a lot. The memory gaps, the voice delay, the weird dreams, the fact that you haven't blinked since the Horus Heresy. You were expecting a dramatic reveal. Choirs maybe. Instead, it's just you, your reflection, and the slow realization that you've been kind of dead for 300 years and still not on break. You nod to yourself, or at least the sarcophagus nods. Close enough. You're a space marine. Now you're a very expensive microwave that punches tanks.
fullTextVi: Bạn chưa được sinh ra. Được rồi, tất nhiên là bạn đã được sinh ra. Đây là Warhammer 40k. Vận may của bạn đã không đưa bạn đến với tư cách là Chúa Giêsu. Bạn sinh ra đã la hét, người đầy máu và có lẽ đã bị phán xét hộp sọ servo với một clipboard. Nhưng phần bạn phải trở thành một con người đã kết thúc nhanh chóng vì ai đó nhìn đứa trẻ 13 tuổi mồ côi, nửa hoang dã của bạn và nghĩ, "Ừ, hãy cho nhổ axit và một bệ phóng tên lửa. " Đầu tiên là các bài kiểm tra, sau đó là phẫu thuật, sau đó là nâng cấp. Họ đã lắp đặt 19 cơ quan. Không phải ẩn dụ. Họ thực sự đã mở mang bạn ra và bắt đầu thêm chúng. Một là cho phép bạn ăn chất độc. Một cho phép bạn thở trong không gian. Một cho phép bạn liếm bụi bẩn và nếm trải cảm giác của nó. Khoa học. Sau đó, họ ghim chiếc carropus đen vào cột sống của bạn, biến cơ thể bạn thành một Cổng USB cho áo giáp điện. Từ thời điểm đó trở đi, bạn không mặc áo giáp. Bạn là áo giáp. Nếu ngứa thì tệ quá. Nếu nó bị chèn ép, đó là lòng trung thành. Họ xóa tên bạn, gọi đó là sự trong sạch. Họ xóa ký ức của bạn. Gọi đó là sự tận tâm. Tính cách của bạn có sự khác biệt không cần thiết. Bạn đã được bổ nhiệm vào một quân đoàn. Không được chọn, không được giao cho ai khác ngoài lính thủy quân lục chiến. Những cái màu xanh. Những người cao quý. Những kẻ in kế hoạch chiến đấu của mình lên giấy da rồi đốt nó lên lửa để thêm độ tinh khiết. Bạn không cảm thấy cao quý. Bạn chỉ cảm thấy nặng nề. Bạn đã gặp đội của mình trong một lồng huấn luyện. Không có tên, chỉ có chuỗi vũ khí và chấn thương. Một trong số họ đã không chớp mắt trong 3 tuần. Một người trích dẫn kinh thánh trong giấc ngủ của mình. Một người cứ nói chuyện với tảng đá của mình như thể đó là người anh em song sinh đã chết của mình. Bạn học nhanh vì đặt câu hỏi khiến bạn bị đánh giá lại và đánh giá lại đồng nghĩa với việc bị đâm và được thay thế bằng lượt xếp hàng tiếp theo. Bạn đã được biết đây là tình anh em. Nó chủ yếu giống như một tổn thương cảm xúc có cấu trúc. Họ dạy bạn cách chiến đấu trước khi bạn học cách ăn chậm. Họ dạy bạn cách tụng kinh trước khi bạn hiểu được một nửa từ. Và khi xương của bạn bị gãy, tốt. Bây giờ bạn có thể học cách chiến đấu trong khi chữa bệnh. Cuối cùng, bạn đã có được lần triển khai đầu tiên. Họ gọi nó là cuộc thập tự chinh vĩ đại. Hàng ngàn thế giới đoàn tụ với Imperium. Hàng ngàn nền văn hóa không muốn trở thành. Bạn đã được yêu cầu mang lại sự đoàn kết. Bạn đã mang đến một sự phẫn nộ và sự phẫn nộ chính đáng. Lần giết đầu tiên của bạn là một kẻ nổi loạn đã gọi hoàng đế được đánh giá cao. Người thứ hai của bạn là một đứa trẻ với khẩu súng plasma và quá nhiều hy vọng. Bạn đã tự nhủ rằng đó là dành cho Imperium. Nó có vị như dầu cháy và sự linh hoạt về mặt đạo đức. Bạn đã nhìn thấy vị nguyên thủy của mình một lần. Rabote Gilaman, đứa con báo thù, được xây dựng như một thánh đường và rực sáng như người luôn nộp thuế sớm. Anh ấy không nhìn thấy bạn. Anh ấy đã nhìn thấy đội hình, nhưng dù sao thì bạn vẫn đứng thẳng. Họ nói ông ấy là cha ruột của bạn. Nhưng bạn không cảm thấy tĩnh lặng, bạn tin vào hoàng đế, vào sứ mệnh, vào ý tưởng rằng tất cả nỗi đau này đều có mục đích. Bởi vì nếu bạn ngừng tin tưởng dù chỉ một giây, bạn có thể sẽ nhớ lại điều đó cảm thấy như được làm người. Và điều đó sẽ tệ hơn. Vì vậy, bạn tiếp tục hành quân, liên tục tự nhủ rằng mọi chuyện vẫn ổn. Và trong một thời gian, nó thực sự có cảm giác như nó đang hoạt động. Hoàng đế đã có một kế hoạch. Thiên hà có một cấu trúc. Đội của bạn chỉ đâm nhau trong lúc tập luyện. Chắc chắn, Cuộc Thập tự chinh vĩ đại chủ yếu là la hét và tuân theo đạn, nhưng ít nhất nó đã được tổ chức la hét. Sau đó, anh họ Legion của bạn đã ngừng trả lời các cuộc gọi Vox. Sau đó, một chiếc khác xuất hiện ở vùng chiến sự với logo mới và kẻ mắt quá nhiều. Sau đó, có người thì thầm: "Nếu bố sai thì sao? " Và điều tiếp theo bạn biết đấy, bạn sẽ được điều động để nhắc nhở những người anh em của mình rằng lòng trung thành có nghĩa là gì với một chiếc tàu chiến. Nhưng này, ít nhất bạn không phải là thuyền trưởng của một tàu chiến 10.000 tấn vượt qua cơn giông bão trong khi né tránh ngư lôi và cố gắng không làm thất vọng người đã chế tạo một nửa Hải quân Hoa Kỳ bất chấp vì đó là trận hải chiến. Và đó là những gì bạn nhận được trong World of Warships, nhà tài trợ ngày nay. Trò chơi chiến thuật miễn phí này cho phép bạn chỉ huy các tàu thực sự của Hoa Kỳ như USS Albany và USS Smith được tái tạo từ bản thiết kế thực tế của thế kỷ 20. Có hơn 40 bản đồ, bảy loại trận chiến và thời tiết thực sự thay đổi bạn chiến đấu. Tàu được chia thành bốn lớp. Thiết giáp hạm đánh mạnh và nhận đòn mạnh hơn. Kẻ hủy diệt rất nhanh, lén lút và dị ứng với việc sống sót. Tàu tuần dương làm một chút việc và bị đổ lỗi khi mọi việc không như ý muốn. Và các nhà cung cấp dịch vụ chỉ cần nhấn nút trên khắp bản đồ và giả vờ đó là chiến lược. Hiện tại, đang có sự kiện ngày 4 tháng 7 với các tàu Hoa Kỳ có thời gian giới hạn, các ngôi sao, da sọc và đủ hỏa lực để khiến ngay cả những người chơi mới cũng trở thành mối đe dọa.
